key_insight: Text-mined clinical knowledge graphs can identify EHR-supported relationships, but causal direction remains uncertain and should not be inferred from diagnosis-coding order alone.
clinical_relevance: Conservatively downgrading uncertain causal claims may help clinical AI systems produce fewer evidence-unsupported answers without sacrificing retrieval recall.
method: Extracted directed candidate relations from 328,839 MIMIC-IV discharge summaries using an LLM and UMLS normalization.
Evaluated co-occurrence lift, diagnosis-coding temporal precedence, and literature corroboration against SemMedDB, with MIMIC-III replication.
Compared lift-only retrieval with conservative causal demotion in a leakage-controlled causal QA benchmark.
evidence_signal: Among 686 candidates with a coding-order direction, agreement with SemMedDB was 54.2% versus 69.4% for extraction; causal demotion reduced evidence-unsupported QA answers from 17.3% to 6.1% while accuracy rose from 35.7% to 37.2%.
watch_item: Co-occurrence support is not causal proof, and literature corroboration covered only 30.4% of candidate relations.
paper_title: Trust the Edge, Doubt the Arrow: Auditing Validation Signals for Text-Mined Clinical Causal Knowledge Graphs
